Mathematics.title: Sorting by Colour
Mathematics.outcome: Put objects with the same colour together.
Mathematics.example: Make one group with 3 red bottle tops and another group with 2 blue bottle tops.
Mathematics.key_idea: Put things with the same colour in one group.

Mathematics.title: Sorting by Shape
Mathematics.outcome: Put objects with the same shape together.
Mathematics.example: Put the circles together. Put the squares in another group.
Mathematics.key_idea: Look at the shape. Put matching shapes together.

Mathematics.title: Sorting by Size
Mathematics.outcome: Put big objects together and small objects together.
Mathematics.example: Put the big leaves in one group and the small leaves in another.
Mathematics.key_idea: Look at how big or small each thing is before you sort it.

Mathematics.title: Grouping the Same Things
Mathematics.outcome: Find things that are the same and put them together.
Mathematics.example: Put all the pencils together. Put all the bottle tops together.
Mathematics.key_idea: Things that are alike belong in the same group.

Mathematics.title: Matching Pairs
Mathematics.outcome: Match each object with one object that goes with it.
Mathematics.example: Give each cup one spoon. Check that every cup has a spoon.
Mathematics.key_idea: Make pairs by matching one thing to one thing.

Mathematics.title: Comparing Groups
Mathematics.outcome: Find which group has more, fewer, or the same number of things.
Mathematics.example: Match one red top to one blue top. See which colour has a top left over.
Mathematics.key_idea: Match things one by one. A leftover thing shows which group has more.

Mathematics.title: Biggest and Smallest
Mathematics.outcome: Find the biggest and the smallest object in a group.
Mathematics.example: Look at three bottles. Point to the biggest bottle, then the smallest.
Mathematics.key_idea: Compare the objects to find the biggest and the smallest.

Mathematics.title: Ordering Small to Big
Mathematics.outcome: Put objects in order from the smallest to the biggest.
Mathematics.example: Line up three sticks: the shortest first and the longest last.
Mathematics.key_idea: Start with the smallest object and finish with the biggest.

Mathematics.title: Ordering Big to Small
Mathematics.outcome: Put objects in order from the biggest to the smallest.
Mathematics.example: Line up three leaves: the biggest first and the smallest last.
Mathematics.key_idea: Start with the biggest object and finish with the smallest.

Mathematics.title: Colour Patterns
Mathematics.outcome: Make and continue a pattern using colours.
Mathematics.example: Put a red top, then a blue top, then red, then blue. What comes next?
Mathematics.key_idea: Look for what repeats. Keep the same order going.

Mathematics.title: Patterns with Objects
Mathematics.outcome: Make and continue a pattern using different objects.
Mathematics.example: Put a pencil, an eraser, a pencil, an eraser. What comes next?
Mathematics.key_idea: Look at the order of the objects. Repeat that order.

Mathematics.title: Counting Forwards and Backwards
Mathematics.outcome: Count forwards and backwards from numbers up to 50.
Mathematics.example: Clap as you count from 21 to 25. Then count backwards from 25 to 21.
Mathematics.key_idea: Say each number in order when you count forwards or backwards.

Mathematics.title: Whole Numbers
Mathematics.outcome: Understand tens and ones, and read and write numbers from 1 to 20.
Mathematics.example: The number 14 is one ten and four ones.
Mathematics.key_idea: Represent a number using tens and ones, and read and write numerals to 20.

Mathematics.title: Fractions: Whole and Half
Mathematics.outcome: Recognise a whole and one-half using practical materials.
Mathematics.example: Fold one sheet of paper into two equal parts to show one-half.
Mathematics.key_idea: A half is one of two equal parts of a whole.

Mathematics.title: Addition
Mathematics.outcome: Add single- and double-digit numbers to a sum of 20 without carrying over.
Mathematics.example: Seven counters and six more counters make 13 counters.
Mathematics.key_idea: Combine groups and find a total no greater than 20 without regrouping.

Mathematics.title: Subtraction
Mathematics.outcome: Subtract numbers up to 20 without borrowing.
Mathematics.example: Taking four objects from a group of 15 leaves 11.
Mathematics.key_idea: Take away the stated amount and count what remains without borrowing.

Mathematics.title: Length
Mathematics.outcome: Compare lengths using non-standard units such as handspans, footsteps, and strides.
Mathematics.example: Measure a mat using handspans, starting each handspan where the last one ended.
Mathematics.key_idea: Measure consistently by repeating the same non-standard unit without gaps or overlaps.

Mathematics.title: Mass
Mathematics.outcome: Compare objects as heavier than, lighter than, or the same as using a simple balance.
Mathematics.example: Place a mango and an orange on opposite sides of a balance beam and observe which side goes down.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use a balance to compare mass and describe the result accurately.

Mathematics.title: Capacity
Mathematics.outcome: Compare container capacities by pouring and describing which holds more or less.
Mathematics.example: Pour water from two cups into the same measuring container to compare their capacities.
Mathematics.key_idea: Compare capacity by using the same method and observing how much each container holds.

Mathematics.title: Time
Mathematics.outcome: Identify days of the week, parts of the day, and sequence daily events.
Mathematics.example: Put waking up, going to school, and going to bed in their usual order.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use day and part-of-day words to describe and sequence events.

Mathematics.title: Money
Mathematics.outcome: Identify Kenyan coins and notes up to KES 100 and take part in small shopping transactions.
Mathematics.example: Choose coins that pay for an item costing KES 20 in a classroom shop.
Mathematics.key_idea: Recognise the printed value of Kenyan money and use it to pay for an item.

Mathematics.title: Lines
Mathematics.outcome: Draw and identify straight and curved lines.
Mathematics.example: Trace the straight edge of a book and draw a curved line around a cup.
Mathematics.key_idea: A straight line does not curve, while a curved line bends.

Mathematics.title: 2D Shapes
Mathematics.outcome: Recognise, name, and sort rectangles, circles, triangles, and squares.
Mathematics.example: Sort paper shapes by name and describe a triangle by its three sides.
Mathematics.key_idea: Identify and sort shapes by their sides and curved boundaries.

English.title: Salutations and Greetings
English.outcome: Use polite words such as good morning, thank you, and please in familiar social situations.
English.example: Greet a classmate by saying, 'Good morning. Please may I join you?'
English.key_idea: Choose a polite greeting or expression that suits the social situation.

English.title: Listening Comprehension
English.outcome: Listen to a short simple story and identify its main characters or sounds.
English.example: After hearing a story about a girl and her dog, name the two characters.
English.key_idea: Listen for story details and use them to identify characters or sounds.

English.title: Phonological Awareness
English.outcome: Recognise and produce letter sounds, rhyming words, and basic word blends.
English.example: Say the first sound in sun, then identify a word that rhymes with sun.
English.key_idea: Listen to sounds in words, including beginning sounds and rhyming endings.

English.title: Pre-Reading Skills
English.outcome: Track print from left to right, handle a book correctly, and turn pages carefully.
English.example: Hold a book the right way up and follow a line of print from left to right.
English.key_idea: Handle a book carefully and follow print from left to right.

English.title: Word Recognition
English.outcome: Read familiar sight words and blend two- to three-letter words.
English.example: Blend the sounds c-a-t to read cat.
English.key_idea: Recognise familiar words and blend letter sounds from left to right.

English.title: Reading Comprehension
English.outcome: Read a short text of two or three sentences with visual prompts and answer direct questions.
English.example: Read a short picture-supported text and answer who is playing.
English.key_idea: Use words and picture clues in a short text to answer direct questions.

English.title: Nouns
English.outcome: Identify common naming words for people and objects in the immediate environment.
English.example: In 'The girl has a book', girl and book are naming words.
English.key_idea: A noun names a person, animal, place, or thing.

English.title: Pronouns
English.outcome: Use the personal pronouns I, you, he, she, and it.
English.example: Use she in 'Amina is kind. She helps.' to refer to Amina.
English.key_idea: Choose a personal pronoun that refers to the person or thing named.

English.title: Verbs
English.outcome: Identify and use simple action words connected to daily routines.
English.example: Run, jump, sit, and eat are action words.
English.key_idea: A verb can tell what a person or thing does.

English.title: Pre-Writing Skills
English.outcome: Practise pattern writing, tracing, and a suitable pencil grip.
English.example: Trace a line of curves while holding a pencil comfortably.
English.key_idea: Practise controlled marks and hold the pencil comfortably.

English.title: Handwriting
English.outcome: Write lowercase and uppercase letters legibly.
English.example: Copy uppercase A and lowercase a carefully onto a line.
English.key_idea: Form uppercase and lowercase letters clearly and consistently.

English.title: Spelling and Guided Writing
English.outcome: Write simple three-letter words and copy short sentences from the board.
English.example: Write the word sun, then copy 'The sun is hot.' with spaces between words.
English.key_idea: Listen for sounds when spelling short words and copy sentences carefully.

Mathematics.title: Number Concept
Mathematics.outcome: Count forward and backward up to 100.
Mathematics.example: Count backwards from 35 to 25 without skipping a number.
Mathematics.key_idea: Keep the counting sequence in order when counting forwards or backwards to 100.

Mathematics.title: Whole Numbers
Mathematics.outcome: Use place value up to hundreds and continue number patterns up to 100.
Mathematics.example: In 246, the digits represent two hundreds, four tens, and six ones.
Mathematics.key_idea: Read each digit by its place and use the pattern rule to continue a sequence.

Mathematics.title: Fractions
Mathematics.outcome: Recognise halves and quarters as equal parts of a whole.
Mathematics.example: Fold a shape into four equal parts; each part is one-quarter.
Mathematics.key_idea: A half has two equal parts in a whole; a quarter has four equal parts.

Mathematics.title: Addition
Mathematics.outcome: Add numbers to a sum of 100 horizontally and vertically, including carrying over.
Mathematics.example: Add 38 and 27 by regrouping ten ones as one ten.
Mathematics.key_idea: Add matching place values and regroup ten ones as one ten when needed.

Mathematics.title: Subtraction
Mathematics.outcome: Subtract numbers up to 100, including basic borrowing or regrouping.
Mathematics.example: To subtract 18 from 42, regroup one ten as ten ones before subtracting the ones.
Mathematics.key_idea: Subtract matching place values and regroup a ten when there are not enough ones.

Mathematics.title: Multiplication
Mathematics.outcome: Understand multiplication as repeated addition for facts up to 5 times 5.
Mathematics.example: Three groups of four counters can be written as 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
Mathematics.key_idea: Represent multiplication with equal groups or repeated addition.

Mathematics.title: Division
Mathematics.outcome: Divide numbers up to 25 by single digits through equal sharing and repeated subtraction.
Mathematics.example: Share 20 counters equally among five learners to find how many each receives.
Mathematics.key_idea: Make equal groups or subtract equal groups repeatedly to divide.

Mathematics.title: Length
Mathematics.outcome: Measure length with fixed arbitrary objects and use the standard unit metre.
Mathematics.example: Measure a desk with the same stick, then compare its length with one metre.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use a consistent unit and describe length in metres when appropriate.

Mathematics.title: Mass
Mathematics.outcome: Measure mass with non-standard items and use the standard unit kilogram.
Mathematics.example: Compare an object with a one-kilogram mass using a balance.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use a balance for comparison and kilogram as a standard mass unit.

Mathematics.title: Capacity
Mathematics.outcome: Measure capacity with smaller containers and use the standard unit litre.
Mathematics.example: Count how many small cups of water fill a one-litre container.
Mathematics.key_idea: Measure liquid capacity consistently and recognise the litre as a standard unit.

Mathematics.title: Time
Mathematics.outcome: Tell time to the hour and half-hour and read months on a calendar.
Mathematics.example: Read 3:30 as half past three and locate a month on a calendar.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use clock hands to read the hour or half-hour and use a calendar to locate months.

Mathematics.title: Money
Mathematics.outcome: Identify Kenyan currency notes up to KES 200, count money, and make change.
Mathematics.example: Pay KES 150 for an item costing KES 120 and calculate the change.
Mathematics.key_idea: Add note values to pay and subtract the cost to find change.

Mathematics.title: Lines
Mathematics.outcome: Identify, sort, and draw vertical, horizontal, and slanted lines.
Mathematics.example: A flagpole is vertical, while the top edge of a table is horizontal.
Mathematics.key_idea: Classify a line by its direction as vertical, horizontal, or slanted.

Mathematics.title: 2D Shapes
Mathematics.outcome: Make patterns with basic 2D shapes and describe their sides and corners.
Mathematics.example: Continue a pattern of triangle, square, triangle, square.
Mathematics.key_idea: Identify a shape pattern and describe shapes by their sides and corners.

English.title: Giving and Following Instructions
English.outcome: Listen to and carry out two-step instructions and simple classroom directions.
English.example: Listen to 'Pick up your book and place it on the desk' and do both steps in order.
English.key_idea: Listen to the full instruction and carry out each step in the order given.

English.title: Oral Expression
English.outcome: Talk about oneself, family, home, and hobbies using complete sentences.
English.example: Say, 'I live with my family, and I enjoy playing football.'
English.key_idea: Share information about familiar topics using complete sentences.

English.title: Phonological Extension
English.outcome: Blend consonant combinations such as ch, sh, br, and fl.
English.example: Blend the sounds in shop or brush to read the word smoothly.
English.key_idea: Say each consonant sound in a blend and combine the sounds to read the word.

English.title: Fluency
English.outcome: Read simple texts aloud with appropriate pacing and basic expression.
English.example: Pause briefly at a full stop while reading a short passage aloud.
English.key_idea: Read accurately at a steady pace and use punctuation to guide expression.

English.title: Vocabulary
English.outcome: Acquire and use thematic words related to home, health, and school.
English.example: Use the word clinic when talking about places that support health.
English.key_idea: Learn new words in a theme and use them in a meaningful sentence.

English.title: Reading Comprehension
English.outcome: Read short paragraphs, answer questions, and predict what may happen next.
English.example: Use a character's actions in a paragraph to predict the next event.
English.key_idea: Use details from the text to answer questions and make a prediction.

English.title: Plurals
English.outcome: Change singular nouns to plurals by adding -s or -es.
English.example: Add -es to box to make boxes.
English.key_idea: Use -s or -es to make the plural form of a familiar noun.

English.title: Articles
English.outcome: Use the articles a and an before singular naming words.
English.example: Write an egg and a book.
English.key_idea: Choose a or an to introduce a singular naming word.

English.title: Prepositions
English.outcome: Use in, on, under, and near to describe spatial relationships.
English.example: The ball is under the chair.
English.key_idea: Choose a preposition that correctly describes where an object is.

English.title: Present Continuous Tense
English.outcome: Use the present continuous forms is walking and are playing.
English.example: The children are playing outside.
English.key_idea: Use am, is, or are with an -ing verb for an action happening now.

English.title: Punctuation
English.outcome: Use capital letters for names and sentence beginnings, and full stops at sentence endings.
English.example: Write 'Musa is here.' with a capital M and a full stop.
English.key_idea: Start a sentence or name with a capital letter and end a statement with a full stop.

English.title: Sentence Construction
English.outcome: Build independent sentences of four to five words using provided keywords.
English.example: Use the words birds, fly, and sky to write 'Birds fly in the sky.'
English.key_idea: Arrange keywords into a complete sentence with a clear meaning.

English.title: Creative Writing
English.outcome: Complete a guided paragraph or fill missing words in a simple story.
English.example: Choose a word to complete a story sentence, then read the paragraph to check its meaning.
English.key_idea: Use story clues to complete missing words and keep ideas connected.

Mathematics.title: Number Concept
Mathematics.outcome: Count forward and backward up to 1,000.
Mathematics.example: Count backwards from 320 to 300, saying each number in sequence.
Mathematics.key_idea: Keep the number sequence in order when counting forwards or backwards to 1,000.

Mathematics.title: Whole Numbers
Mathematics.outcome: Use place value up to thousands and continue number patterns up to 1,000.
Mathematics.example: In 3,472, the digits represent three thousands, four hundreds, seven tens, and two ones.
Mathematics.key_idea: Read digits by their place value and use a pattern rule to continue a sequence.

Mathematics.title: Fractions
Mathematics.outcome: Recognise halves, quarters, and eighths as parts of a whole or a group.
Mathematics.example: Divide eight equal counters into two groups to show one-half of the group.
Mathematics.key_idea: Name a fraction by the number of equal parts in the whole or group.

Mathematics.title: Addition
Mathematics.outcome: Add numbers up to 1,000, including three-digit numbers with regrouping.
Mathematics.example: Add 268 and 157 by regrouping ones and tens as needed.
Mathematics.key_idea: Add matching place values and regroup when a place has ten or more.

Mathematics.title: Subtraction
Mathematics.outcome: Subtract numbers up to 1,000 using borrowing or regrouping.
Mathematics.example: Subtract 186 from 423 by regrouping a hundred or ten when needed.
Mathematics.key_idea: Subtract by place value and regroup when there are not enough units in a place.

Mathematics.title: Multiplication
Mathematics.outcome: Use multiplication tables from 1 through 10 with arrays and equal groupings.
Mathematics.example: An array with four rows of six counters represents 4 times 6.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use equal groups, arrays, or known facts to find a product.

Mathematics.title: Division
Mathematics.outcome: Understand division as the inverse of multiplication and divide up to 90 by single digits without remainders.
Mathematics.example: Since 7 times 8 equals 56, 56 divided by 7 equals 8.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use the related multiplication fact to solve a division problem.

Mathematics.title: Length
Mathematics.outcome: Measure and record length accurately in metres.
Mathematics.example: Measure a classroom wall in metres and record the unit with the measurement.
Mathematics.key_idea: Measure from the zero point and record the measurement with its unit.

Mathematics.title: Mass
Mathematics.outcome: Measure, compare, and estimate mass using kilograms.
Mathematics.example: Estimate a bag's mass, then compare it with a one-kilogram reference mass.
Mathematics.key_idea: Estimate first, then use a suitable kilogram measure or balance to check.

Mathematics.title: Capacity
Mathematics.outcome: Measure liquid capacity in litres and add or subtract capacities in practical activities.
Mathematics.example: Combine 2 litres and 3 litres of water to find a total of 5 litres.
Mathematics.key_idea: Use litres consistently and add or subtract amounts with the same unit.

Mathematics.title: Time
Mathematics.outcome: Tell time to the nearest five minutes and relate hours, minutes, days, and weeks.
Mathematics.example: Read 2:25 to the nearest five minutes and recall that one hour has 60 minutes.
Mathematics.key_idea: Read the clock in five-minute intervals and use known time-unit relationships.

Mathematics.title: Money
Mathematics.outcome: Use Kenyan currency notes up to KES 1,000 to calculate shopping costs and balances.
Mathematics.example: Add the prices of two items, pay with a note, and calculate the balance due.
Mathematics.key_idea: Find the total cost first, then subtract it from the amount paid to find the balance.

Mathematics.title: Lines
Mathematics.outcome: Identify parallel, intersecting, and perpendicular lines in the environment and in drawings.
Mathematics.example: The opposite edges of a rectangular book cover are parallel; adjacent edges meet at right angles.
Mathematics.key_idea: Compare line direction and check whether intersecting lines meet at a right angle.

Mathematics.title: 3D Shapes and Models
Mathematics.outcome: Create 3D models or patterns from 2D shapes and identify cubes, cuboids, cylinders, and spheres.
Mathematics.example: Sort a box, tin, and ball as cuboid, cylinder, and sphere.
Mathematics.key_idea: Identify a solid by observing its faces, curved surfaces, and overall form.

English.title: Public Speaking and Etiquette
English.outcome: Give a short presentation, describe events, and take turns during conversations.
English.example: Describe a school event to the class and listen respectfully when another learner speaks.
English.key_idea: Organise a short oral description and take turns respectfully.

English.title: Debate and Discussion
English.outcome: Ask and answer higher-order questions about local current events or school activities.
English.example: Ask why a school activity is useful and support an answer with a reason.
English.key_idea: Ask thoughtful questions and support opinions with relevant reasons.

English.title: Independent Reading
English.outcome: Read level-appropriate storybooks silently for pleasure and information.
English.example: Choose a suitable storybook, read quietly, and identify one interesting fact or event.
English.key_idea: Choose a suitable text and read independently to understand or enjoy it.

English.title: Advanced Comprehension
English.outcome: Identify themes, draw conclusions, and discuss lessons from stories.
English.example: Use a character's choices and story events to explain a lesson learned.
English.key_idea: Use evidence from the story to explain its theme or a conclusion.

English.title: Simple Past Tense
English.outcome: Use simple past-tense verbs such as walked, played, and went.
English.example: Change 'I walk to school' to 'I walked to school yesterday.'
English.key_idea: Use a past-tense verb for an action that happened before now.

English.title: Conjunctions
English.outcome: Join ideas using and, but, and because.
English.example: Join two ideas: 'I wore a coat because it was cold.'
English.key_idea: Choose a conjunction that shows how the ideas are connected.

English.title: Adjectives
English.outcome: Describe nouns using attributes such as colour, size, and quantity.
English.example: In 'a big red ball', big and red describe the ball.
English.key_idea: Use an adjective to give a relevant detail about a noun.

English.title: Possessives
English.outcome: Use possessive words such as my, your, his, her, ours, and theirs correctly.
English.example: Use her to show that a book belongs to a girl: 'This is her book.'
English.key_idea: Choose a possessive word that shows who owns or is connected to something.

English.title: Paragraph Writing
English.outcome: Write a structured paragraph of three to five coherent sentences about a theme.
English.example: Write connected sentences about My School, keeping each sentence on the same topic.
English.key_idea: Keep three to five related sentences focused on one theme.

English.title: Functional Writing
English.outcome: Write simple messages, invitations, and lists.
English.example: Write a short invitation that tells the reader what the event is and when it happens.
English.key_idea: Choose the details and format that suit the message, invitation, or list.

English.title: Punctuation
English.outcome: Use question marks for questions and commas to separate items in a list.
English.example: Write 'Do you want mangoes, bananas, or oranges?' with commas in the list and a question mark at the end.
English.key_idea: Use a question mark for a direct question and commas between list items.
